text: It was now fully night. <break time="0.8s" /> And a thick, humid fog. <break time="0.8s" /> That had hung over the city. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon ended in a settled and heavy rain. <break time="0.8s" /> So I tied a handkerchief about my mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> And kept on. <break time="0.8s" /> For half an hour. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man held his way with difficulty. <break time="0.8s" /> Along the great thoroughfare. <break time="0.8s" /> And though I walked close at his elbow. <break time="0.8s" /> He never once turned round. <break time="0.8s" /> To look at me. <break time="0.8s" /> Turning into a side street that was less crowded. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked more slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> And with less object than before crossing and recrossing the way. <break time="0.8s" /> Without any apparent aim. <break time="0.8s" /> At length he entered a square. <break time="0.8s" /> Brilliantly lighted and overflowing with life. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he walked round and round. <break time="0.8s" /> For another hour. <break time="0.8s" /> His chin sunk upon his breast. <break time="0.8s" /> And his eyes rolling wildly. <break time="0.8s" /> Over the faces around him. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he hurried into a vast bazaar. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he passed from shop to shop. <break time="0.8s" /> Priced nothing, spoke no word. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked at all the objects. <break time="0.8s" /> With a wild and vacant stare. <break time="0.8s" /> When a loud toned clock struck eleven. <break time="0.8s" /> A shopkeeper. <break time="0.8s" /> While putting up a shutter. <break time="0.8s" /> Jostled the old man. <break time="0.8s" /> And at that instant. <break time="0.8s" /> A strong shudder ran through his whole frame. <break time="0.8s" /> Rushing through a maze of crooked lanes. <break time="0.8s" /> He reached one of the principal theatres. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as it was closing. <break time="0.8s" /> And plunged eagerly into the audience. <break time="0.8s" /> As they poured out through the doors. <break time="0.8s" /> He seemed to gasp for breath. <break time="0.8s" /> As he threw himself amid the crowd. <break time="0.8s" /> But the intense agony of his countenance. <break time="0.8s" /> Had, I thought, in some measure abated. <break time="0.8s" /> As if the crowd itself gave him relief.
